lessons: Found by DOGFOODING the skill against our own site (agentskills.co.il) rather than by any gate: the skill stated 'Set x-default to the English version' as an absolute rule. Google's own spec defines x-default as matching any language not explicitly listed, and says nothing about English. The rule would have led an agent to 'fix' a correct Israel-first configuration into a worse one. Softened to an audience-dependent decision. LESSON: absolute rules about another vendor's spec are the same defect class as PermaBot and the Brave claim; check whether the spec actually mandates what the skill asserts.

seo_audit.py sent 'User-Agent: SEO-Audit/1.0' and was refused by real sites, including our own, reporting a bare 'Could not fetch URL'. This blocked two genuine audits before anyone treated it as a bug. Now sends a browser UA with the tool name appended, plus Accept and Accept-Language headers, and reports the actual failure reason on stderr.

The TLS branch as first written caught ssl.SSLError directly, which never fires because urllib wraps it in URLError. Caught only by running the script against a real failing host. LESSON: exception branches need to be exercised, not just written.
Running the skill on our own project surfaced more real defects in one pass than the automated review gates did. Dogfood every skill against agentskills.co.il as a standing step.

Shipped 2.3.0 without an independent reviewer: all four review subagents went idle without returning output. A /code-review pass afterwards found 4 real defects. LESSON: when the verification panel does not return, the mechanical gates are NOT a substitute for an independent read, and the honest move is to hold or to get a review by another route BEFORE pushing, not after.

seo_audit.py checked for bot NAMES appearing anywhere in robots.txt rather than parsing rules. This meant a bot under 'Disallow: /' counted as present (our own agentskills.co.il robots.txt reported GPTBot as present while actually blocking it), and the most damaging misconfiguration, an explicitly blocked Claude-SearchBot, produced NO warning at all. Replaced with a real group parser resolving allow/disallow per user agent, including wildcard fallback and longest-match precedence.

I extended an inherited substring heuristic instead of fixing it. LESSON: when adding a check on top of existing logic, verify the existing logic is sound first; extending a broken check inherits and amplifies the bug.

'Hebrew supported since Nov 2025' for AI Mode was both unsourced AND wrong: Google's own post is dated Oct 07 2025. The substance held up (Hebrew and Israel are both on Google's AI Mode availability list) but the date was invented. Replaced with the sourced availability statement. Same defect class as the '30-day freshness' figure removed in 2.3.0.

evidence.json still cited platform.openai.com and support.anthropic.com in three PRE-EXISTING claims after 2.3.0 fixed those URLs in the prose. LESSON: a URL migration must sweep evidence.json too, not just the body; otherwise evidence and body cite different canonical sources for the same fact.
Bootstrapped references/domain-checklist.md and this log; neither existed before v2.3.0, so prior cycles had no cross-cycle memory and no expert-review anchor.

Root cause of this cycle's CRITICAL: the skill documented the GPTBot/OAI-SearchBot training-vs-search split correctly for OpenAI but never re-checked whether other vendors had adopted the same split. Anthropic added Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User (docs updated ~Feb 2026) and the skill kept recommending ClaudeBot alone. NEXT CYCLE: re-enumerate EVERY vendor's full documented bot list from the vendor's own page, do not spot-check the one bot already named.

Two cited vendor doc URLs had 301-redirected to new hosts (platform.openai.com -> developers.openai.com, support.anthropic.com -> support.claude.com) while still returning 200 through the redirect, so link validation passed and hid the move. NEXT CYCLE: check final resolved URL, not just status code.

references/platform-algorithms.md contained a fabricated Bing crawler name (PermaBot) that survived multiple cycles because reference files are rarely re-read. The evidence gate did not catch it because user-agent tokens are not numeric and were never extracted as claims. Consider whether bot names should be evidence-tracked.

Deferred: FAQPage is recommended throughout without noting that Google restricted FAQ RICH RESULTS to authoritative government and health sites in 2023. Logged in domain-checklist.md under Should-cover; the schema still has AI-extraction value, so this is a framing fix, not a removal.

UNVERIFIED and deliberately NOT written this cycle: the claim that ChatGPT with browsing prefers its cached index over re-fetching a supplied URL. Plausible and repeated by third parties, but no primary source found. Revisit.

RESOLVED this cycle (not deferred after all): the unsourced '30-day freshness' figure was removed from all 5 occurrences across SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md, seo-checklist.md and platform-algorithms.md, and replaced with non-numeric guidance. It was the same class of untraceable vendor stat that earlier cycles stripped from the GEO tables, so leaving it would have been inconsistent.
